feat(web): Umami analytics on agentcut.studio

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(web): sign in on our own page, with an email and a code

/login is the site's own two-step form instead of Clerk's Account Portal, whose GitHub
button led to a 404 and whose look was not the site's. public/login.js runs it with
Clerk's browser library from the instance's Frontend API: the email_code first factor
for a known address, a sign-up with an email code for a new one, then setActive, which
leaves the __session cookie the server already verifies. The GitHub connection is
disabled in Clerk until it is wanted.

styles.css and login.js are now linked with a hash of their contents and served
immutable: Cloudflare had kept a four-hour-old stylesheet in front of every deploy.
AGENT-FIRST row 163.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(web): any account submits any public repository, listed under its GitHub owner

Signing in is by email for now, so GitHub no longer gates submitting: a private
repository is still refused, but the repository's owner is no longer compared with the
person's GitHub login. An account without GitHub is a users row with a NULL login
(migration 0003). A listing shows the repository's GitHub owner and picture as who made
it; the account that submitted it first is the one offered Check for updates and
Remove. AGENT-FIRST row 162, amending 158.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(web): /login reaches Clerk's sign-in page

A request's auth state only carries a sign-in URL when one is passed in, so asking it
returned nothing and /login said "Sign-in did not start" on the live instance. The URL
now comes from Clerk's own redirect (createRedirect, from the publishable key): the
Account Portal at accounts.agentcut.studio, with the page to come back to. The docs
record the production instance: email sign-in for now, GitHub linkable once its
OAuth credentials are set, and the CNAMEs in the zone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(web): the marketplace is live at agentcut.studio, served from the owner's box

The same Hono app, with node around it instead of workerd: src/node.ts fills the
bindings from the environment, serves public/ itself and restores the scheme nginx
terminated, so canonical URLs and a form's Origin check are the address the browser
used. scripts/build-server.mjs inlines everything into one file, so the box runs node
and installs nothing. deploy/ holds pm2 (agentcut-web on 3013), the nginx vhost, the
one-time setup and the deploy script; the database is a TCP connection beside it, so
there is no Hyperdrive certificate to keep in date. wrangler.jsonc stays for pnpm dev
and the tests. MARKET_URL points at the live domain; AGENT-FIRST row 161 records it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(packs): a pack carries pictures of what it makes, a cover and up to eight screenshots

Without pictures the packs looked flat. pack.json now names a `cover` and
`screenshots` (png, jpg, webp or gif, 5 MB each), a rule in PackManifest so the
importer, the export and the marketplace refuse the same things.

- Marketplace: checked like any named file, refused over 5 MB, served from
  GitHub at the pinned commit. Cards lead with the cover; a pack's page shows
  the cover and the screenshots at their own shape. Migration 0002 keeps the
  latest cover on the pack row.
- Studio: the cover in the marketplace list, cover and screenshots in the
  import preview (/api/packs/preview-image reads only what the manifest names),
  copied into the pack's folder by role on install before anything else is
  written, edited on the pack's page, carried by export.
- Agent: packs.images.get | add | remove, the same functions as the panel.
- news-desk, showcase and stream-shorts carry stills of real renders of their
  own templates; versions bumped so the marketplace registers them.

AGENT-FIRST row 160; PACKS.md → Pictures.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(market): the marketplace's database is Postgres on the owner's server, through Hyperdrive

D1 is gone. apps/web keeps users, packs and pack_versions in the `agentcut`
database on the owner's shared Postgres host (role agentcut_app, connection
limit 20, CONNECT revoked from every other role; schema already applied).

- One `postgres` client per request on the HYPERDRIVE binding, closed after
  the response. Registering a version and repointing the pack at its highest
  version is one transaction.
- scripts/migrate.mjs is the one migration runner, for production, the local
  database and the tests, recorded in schema_migrations.
- `pnpm dev` and the 21 end-to-end tests run against PGlite behind a socket,
  reached through wrangler's local Hyperdrive: the same binding and driver as
  production, offline, nothing to install. Search stays case-insensitive.
- README's Deploy covers the Coolify CA (Hyperdrive verifies it) and
  --caching-disabled (Hyperdrive does not invalidate reads on a write).

AGENT-FIRST row 159; SPEC S11 and AGENTS.md amended.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(market): a pack is a GitHub repository, and only submitting one needs an account

The marketplace stops storing packs and starts pointing at them. A listed pack is a
public repository (or a folder in one) pinned to a commit, and the `source` it hands
out is raw.githubusercontent at that SHA — a URL `packs.inspect` and `packs.import`
already read, so installing is unchanged.

Submitting at /submit reads pack.json at the head of the branch, validates it with the
same PackManifest the app imports with, checks every file it names is in the commit's
tree, and refuses a repository the signed-in GitHub account does not own. Check for
updates re-reads the branch and registers a bumped version; a version already
registered is never re-pinned.

Accounts are Clerk's, and they are needed for exactly three writes — submit, update,
remove. Browsing, searching and installing are anonymous, and with no Clerk keys
configured every visitor is a local identity, so a checkout never asks anybody to sign
in.

Gone with this: R2 and the upload path, sessions and our own GitHub OAuth, API tokens,
device codes, /device, /r/, `agentcut login | logout | whoami` and `agentcut packs
publish` — now `packs submit`, which opens the form. Ranking shows GitHub stars,
because GitHub serves the files and there is no download of ours to count.

AGENT-FIRST row 158, and the amendments it makes to row 156 and SPEC S11.

feat: one workspace of apps and packages; a 2 MB CLI that fetches the rest

The single Next app becomes a pnpm workspace (SPEC S11):

- apps/studio: the visual editor, its routes, views, components and hooks
- apps/web: the landing page and the packs marketplace on Cloudflare Workers, D1 and R2
- packages/core: the editor without a face — types, data, lib and server code of every
  module, shared by the studio, the CLI and the marketplace's upload checks
- packages/render: the Remotion compositions
- packages/cli: `agentcut` on npm, bundled with esbuild

`npm i -g agentcut` installs about 2 MB. ffmpeg, the renderer (with Remotion's
compositor and browser) and the standalone studio download on first use into
~/.agentcut/runtime, pinned to the CLI's version, verified against the registry's
sha512, with a progress bar (common/server/runtime.ts). `agentcut` alone opens the
studio. A checkout downloads nothing and keeps workspace/ beside the code.

The marketplace (AGENT-FIRST row 156): a free registry with accounts and a device-code
login for the CLI. A marketplace pack is a URL packs.inspect and packs.import already
read, so finding one is the only new path: Settings → Packs → Import, the agent's
packs.search, and `agentcut packs search | install | publish`.

Also: Remotion and ffmpeg load in one place each, so they stay out of the CLI bundle
and the studio's trace; root.ts keeps WORKSPACE lazy for code that only needs ffmpeg;
the architecture test holds core free of React and the heavy runtime; render-parity
now expects only the edited video's export to go stale (row 155).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(render): an export stays downloadable until its own video changes

Downloads were valid only at the project revision they were rendered at, so fixing
one word in one of 104 videos took all 55 rendered downloads away. Each rendered.json
entry now records its video's content signature (moved to editor/server/signature from
publishing), and renderedClips and pinExport take an export as current while its own
video still signs the same. Unsigned entries keep the revision rule. The check runs
once per revision, since downloads are served range by range.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(glossary): a phrase wins over a word inside it

"Cloud" is a mishearing of Claude, so "Cloud Run" came out as "Claude Run" in the
transcript text even with Cloud Run in the glossary: the one-word alias ran after the
phrase. Phrases are applied again last, so the longer term stands.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(templates): a restatement may add words, and its cut ends where the sound starts

A comment read twice, the second time as "entre el Claude o el Codex de 20 dólares
para Deska", never reached seven identical words in a row. The second reading may now
add up to three words of its own, never dropping one of the first's, both starting on
the same word. And the cut ends at the quietest moment in the 0.3 s before the second
reading: its first word, timed 80 ms late, had lost a syllable.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(templates): a passage said again to say it better loses the first saying

A viewer's comment read twice, the first time stumbling, survived every pass: the
first reading finishes its sentence, so the abandoned-take rules let it through. The
retake pass now also cuts a restatement — seven or more words said word for word
again within 20 s, the repeated run at least 0.4 of what came before the second take —
keeping the second. A take squeezed faster than 0.12 s a word was written twice by the
transcript, not said twice, and neither retake rule cuts audio under it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(clips): a clip a few words short of its full stop runs on to it

"…es la referencia para que te" ended a clip one second before "construya cosas
buenas." closed the point. tightenBoundaries now carries the end to a full stop at
most six words away with no pause over a second on the way; a clip that already ends
a sentence, or a transcript without punctuation, ends where it was told.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(clips): open on the clip's own sentence, and cut a muted pause the aligner hid in a word

A clip opened on "el certificado.", the end of the previous answer, then held nine
seconds of a muted mic before the question. tightenBoundaries now drops the tail of a
sentence begun before the clip (up to six words ending in a full stop) and opens on the
next one; without punctuation nothing moves. silenceCuts caps a word at 1.5 s when
proposing a pause and listens from the start of a word longer than that, so the 8.3 s
the aligner gave "certificado." is found and cut only where the sound is quiet.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(captions): a clip's words are heard whole, and a phrase said twice pairs with the one heard

Hearing a line-timed transcript's stretch ran whisper with VAD. Token times come back
on the stitched speech and rebaseOntoSource lays them back by estimate; next to a pause
that moved words across it. On a real clip "un MVP" was captioned 1.5 s late, past the
silence, with the rest of the sentence after it, and the template's silence cut then
removed the gap where it had been said. A clip's stretch is talking, so it is now heard
without VAD (vad: false) and its times are the source's own. The provided record
carries heardWith; a stretch heard another way is heard again.

pairWords breaks ties between pairings that agree on as many words by time, so
"lo que se le... lo que yo le llamo" heard as one "lo que" pairs with the second,
said where it was heard, instead of squeezing the restart into 0.4 s after the pause.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(preview): an autoplaying preview starts once its footage has loaded, instead of freezing on frame 0

Remotion's autoPlay starts the clock while the source is still buffering and the
clock stays at 0:00 with the button reading "playing"; captions never come up
because the frame never moves. Play through the ref once the first load settles.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(review): swipe deck to approve or reject videos full screen, with the agent beside the card

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(captions): stream captions come up when the words are said, and the lit word has room

A transcript timed per line (Restream's: one whole-second time per line) had its
words spread over each line by length, which inside a long line with a pause put
words up to two seconds from where they are said: the phrase was on screen,
waiting, before it was spoken. Now every stretch a timeline uses is heard by the
recogniser (timeProvidedWords) — at clip selection before boundaries are settled,
on Re-sync captions / transcript.resync, and when imported media takes its words —
and each word takes the time it was heard at (timeFromHeard). The text never
changes; stretches heard are recorded so none is heard twice. On 68 s of a real
stream, lines up more than 0.3 s early went from 24 of 42 to 1 of 43.

The lit caption word scaled 8% over a bare 0.28em gap, so long words ran into
their neighbours ("básicamente referenciando" read as one word). Every word now
keeps 0.08em of room either side and the lit word grows only into it (litScale);
fitRows counts the room. Nothing moves when the lit word changes.

AGENT-FIRST rows 150 and 151; row 138 amended.

useProjectStream polls it every second, at once on focus.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(packs): a pack may carry code — edit-time recipes, trusted by hash, run sandboxed — and the showcase pack ships the first three

A pack's recipes are ES modules that build parts of a video through the editor's own
tools (project.read/edit, the resolved timeline, an upload and ffmpeg in scratch), so
what they make is ordinary EDL that renders offline and can be changed by hand.
Nothing runs until the owner trusts the exact sha256 of the code, from the pack's page
or `agentcut packs trust`; no tool trusts, so an agent cannot. A run is a child
`node --permission` reading only its pack, scratch and font folders, with no network,
children or environment. Reachable from Video → Pack recipes, packs.recipes.run
(agent/MCP) and `agentcut packs run`. Decision 143; rows 44, 72 and 100 amended.

packs/showcase packages the model-comparison video: style guide, review, template,
a CC0 dramatic bed, and the teaser, camera-intro and jump-card recipes, which rebuilt
the approved opening of the día 176 video frame for frame.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(transcription): re-importing a transcript keeps words a person corrected by hand

Every re-import re-cut every shot's words from the transcript, so correcting a clip's
words by hand (a name merged, a word re-timed, a misspoken number taken out) was undone
the next time the glossary grew — on every clip at once. A shot whose words no longer
match the previous transcript was corrected by hand: it keeps its words and only takes
the glossary. Untouched shots take the new words as before. One rule (freshWords) for
the source and for imported media.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(rules): a phrase misheard as a phrase of as many words is corrected on the caption words too

"la guía" is how the recogniser heard "la IA" all through a stream, but a glossary
phrase only corrected segment text, so the captions kept it — and "guía" alone cannot
be the alias, because "una guía" is a guide. A multi-word alias whose term has as many
words now replaces the timed words one for one, keeping their punctuation; nothing
merges, so no caption moves. Phrases of another length stay text-only, as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(stream-comments): a message read from the backlog is found, and has to be read out in full to count

A stream reads its chat late: "sabes otra alternativa barata a Cursor?" was read seven
and a half minutes after it arrived, past both the three minutes the selection looked
and the four the template did, so its clip went out without its card. The reach is now
fifteen minutes (comment.lookbackSec 900 in the pack), and a message read more than
four minutes after it arrived must be heard at least three of its words — "ya volvió"
said ten minutes on is a coincidence.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(stream-comments): a comment card sits between the hook and the captions, never across them

A long message is a tall card, and centred at a fixed height it lay across the caption
band. The card is now placed by its real size (read from the PNG): moved up until its
bottom clears the top of the captions, kept below a hook held at the top, and drawn
narrower when there is not room for it. Checked on the stream's tallest card, whose
exported frame shows it clear of both.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(stream-comments): a pop comment lands within the first second and is gone by about the third

On the stream's clips: one that talks for five seconds before the message is read left
the viewer without the question until 4.8 s, and a long message kept its card up for
five. comment.latestSec (1 s) is the latest it lands and comment.maxSeconds (2.4 s in
the pack) the longest it stays; the captions carry the rest of the reading.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(templates,agent): a hook after an intro is the template's own, and the editing agent leaves exports and the owner's files alone

- templateItemState read any hook, watermark or music bed not starting at zero as moved
  by a person — but a template starts them after its intro card, so re-applying kept
  the old hook and stacked a second one. They are the template's where the body starts.
- The editing agent imported a finished export as the source of a "new version" (a
  zoom into the camera corner, a second hook, a second end card) and copied its render
  over the owner's file in Downloads. Its prompt now says an export is finished, a new
  version is made from what the export was made of, and nothing outside its folder is
  written, copied, moved or deleted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(assets,project): a missing asset is never cached, and a stopped job's stage is not shown as the project's

- /api/assets/<id>/file marked every response immutable for a year, the 404 for a file
  briefly away included: the preview kept a restored comment card off the video for good
  while the export, which asks again, showed it. Only a served file is kept now.
- The project badge showed the last job's stage even after it was stopped ("rendering
  1/50" on a ready project); it shows a job's stage only while the job runs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(clipping,rules): an analysis no longer freezes the workspace glossary into the project, and a phrase correction is not said twice

- selectClips runs in the project folder and wrote its copy of the merged glossary and
  preferences as glossary.json and preferences.md — the project-level settings' own
  names. Every analysis froze them into a project override, so the owner's later
  corrections ("Codets" is Codex, "CloudCode" is Claude Code) silently never applied.
  The copies are now selection-glossary.json and selection-preferences.md.
- A one-word mishearing of a phrase ("ILA" for "la IA") no longer repeats the phrase's
  first word when it was just said: "con ILA" is "con la IA", "la ILA" is "la IA".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(stream-comments,transcription): a reading is the stretch saying most of the message, and a fitted word never spans a silence

Both found on the first clips cut from a real stream:

- "…la app de Claude", six seconds of silence, then "¿Qué dura más, Codex 100 dólares o
  Claude de 100…" read out: readingSpan took the stray Claude as the start, so the agent
  was told the wrong second and the card showed before the message was read. A reading
  is now the stretch of unbroken speech saying the most of the message's words (two at
  least), extended only by words not yet said, from the start of its phrase.
- spreadOverSpeech could stretch a word across a silence inside one transcript line:
  "Claude" claimed the six seconds of dead air, so the pause was never cut and the card
  held for eight seconds. A word now keeps the side of the silence holding most of it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(transcription): a transcript can be handed over before the first analysis, and the owner's glossary spells its names

Both found importing a real stream's transcript into a new project:

- A project has no edit list until its first analysis, which is exactly when the
  panel offers Add transcript: the import wrote the transcript and then failed putting
  words on clips that did not exist, and the panel's state failed the same way.
- The transcript wrote "Cloud"/"Cloudde" 79 times for Claude and "Desca" 86 times
  for Deska, so captions read wrong and "pagas claude?" was never matched as read out.
  The owner's glossary is their own and deterministic; it is now the one pass a
  provided transcript gets. The proofreading model still never touches it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(clipping): the selection agent reads the chat, and the chat's own cards become the comments

- chat.txt: every message on the video's clock, with the second it was read out loud,
  read-outs first; the clips prompt makes a question read out and answered the first
  material, starting half a second before the reading.
- The unified chat's export (clips/<stream>/messages.json + cards/) is a chat source,
  and a message it drew is placed as that picture, byte for byte.
- Line-timed transcripts read [Speaker 1] as the speaker, and a line lasts what it takes
  to say rather than until the next line.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs(templates): the end card plays alone, and an upright source is framed whole

Records what 2a53608 made true: the body ends at any Outro on the main track, so no
hook or card is held over the end card, and a portrait source is never split.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(templates): an end card already on the video ends the hook, and an upright source is never split

Found on a real edit: an agent imported a finished vertical short as its source and
applied the stream template again. The split cut the stream's camera corner out of
an upright frame — a zoom into the wall — and the hook ran over the end card, because
the body only ended at an outro this application added, not one already pinned there.

The body now ends at any Outro on the main track (and starts after any Intro), and
layoutFor frames a portrait source whole instead of splitting it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(stream-comments): the pop comment arrives in a tenth of a second, coming into focus

The reference shorts do not cut the card in: it slides in from a little to the right,
half-seen and out of focus, and is sharp on the third frame; it leaves into focus
lost the same way. blur gains a ramp (hold / out / in), editable in the inspector,
and the card carries one of each; its keyframes keep it at full size, which is how a
pop is told from an open comment (isPopComment). A template laying the blur again
under a person's pop keeps the card's own arrival and exit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(clipping): a clip ends where the last word's sound stops, and a pop-comment clip keeps its opening beat

A proposal ending on the recogniser's end for "rápido." (2033.40) kept "rapi": the
sound ran to 2033.76. tightenBoundaries now takes the source's speech runs and follows
the last word's run to where it stops (+80 ms, within 0.6 s, never into the next
word), and reaches the first word back to its onset. selectClips reads them from the
project's audio, extracting it once when a provided transcript left none.

A clip judged under a rule that puts a pop comment on it keeps delaySec of the
silence before the reading, so the message lands after a beat of clip and hook
instead of on the first frame.

Checked on dia-174 with the channel's own rules: 2002.45 -> 2033.98, the comment at
0.61 s, "rápido." whole, then the 6 PM card.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(stream-comments): the viewer's message pops in over the hook while it is read out

A stream short that reads a viewer out, measured off a reference: the clip and its
hook first; ~0.6 s in the chat bubble lands with a bubble-burst over a blurred frame,
held while the streamer reads it and gone on the frame they finish; the hook never
leaves and the captions never stop.

- comment.style "pop" (and card "chat", delaySec, followReading, blur, sound) on
  TemplateComment; the math lives in templates/lib/comment.ts, shared by the template
  and comments.place, which takes style — the panel's Pops in over it / Opens the video.
- readingSpan times the card to the reading: each of the message's words once, ending
  when the answer starts reusing them.
- A blur edit type: a shot's picture and overlays, never its captions. Editable in the
  inspector and the timeline like a punch-in.
- The bubble starter sound, and starter sounds a later version ships now reach an
  existing library without resurrecting deleted ones.
- stream-shorts 1.1.0 uses the pop; clip counts go to 200 per run.

Checked on a real stream: dia-174 against its own chat found "pagas claude?" and
rendered the card at 0.61 -> 3.01 s (reference 0.64 -> 3.00), pop at -1.4 dBFS.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(transcription): a transcript you already have is the source of truth, and whisper steps aside

perf(render): cut out the footage a video plays before rendering it

The 26-minute export that died on frame one was not seeking slowly. Remotion's
`OffthreadVideo` does not stream: the first frame naming a source sends its proxy
to copy that whole file into a temp directory before a single pixel comes back,
and its downloader accepts nothing but http(s) — so serving the workspace over
loopback, the only way to hand it a five-hour recording at all, cannot get out of
the copy. Five hours were being copied to read 26 minutes of them, and the
half-minute default expired somewhere in the middle of it. That default is a day
now, which stopped the export failing; this stops it being absurd.

The stretches the timeline actually plays are cut out with ffmpeg first, merged
where they nearly meet, and the composition is pointed at those. The recording is
never copied, and every frame after the first seeks inside minutes rather than
hours — the cuts carry a keyframe a second, which is the other half of it.

Nothing about the project changes. The EDL is the authority and is not rewritten;
only the props handed to one render are, and a shot's times move by exactly what
its footage moved. Everything else about a clip — the crop in source pixels, the
words and edits in clip-relative seconds — is measured from the shot's own start
and needs no adjusting. A render test holds that down by exporting the same
revision twice, once through the source and once through the cuts, and comparing
the pixels.

Cutting is re-encoded rather than copied on purpose: `-c copy` starts at the
keyframe before the cut, leaving an offset nothing downstream could learn without
probing the result. And it only happens where it pays — a source under a quarter
gigabyte, or one the video plays most of, is left exactly as it was, which is
every project of ordinary files.

astats resets once per audio frame and a decoded frame is about 23ms, so the pass
printed 7.2kB of metadata per second of audio: 114MB for the four-hour stream in

  analyze job already has.

  keeps the loudest rather than the first 400 in time order — which, at a reading
  every 23ms, would have described a four-hour stream by its opening minutes even if
  the pass had worked. Same source: 400 peaks, first at 0:00:31, last at 4:22:33,

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(preview): a cut arrives on the next picture instead of on black

Some clips flashed black on every cut; the ones that never cut never did. An
export was never affected — it extracts frames off-thread — and the one-frame
black at a splice fixed in 63c3a6e is a different fault. This one is the Player.

A cut, whether a shot boundary or the splice a silence leaves, mounts a brand new
`<video>` on the source. That element starts from nothing: it reads the header of
a multi-hour recording, seeks hours in, and paints nothing until a frame decodes.
Three things made that take seconds instead of milliseconds, and a fourth let the
clock run straight through it.

- `media/[mediaId]` answered every byte range with a full `readEditor`, which
  validates the entire edit list. On the four-hour project measured, one 4KB range
  took 2.5 to 4.2 seconds, and a `<video>` asks for many before its first frame.
  `mediaFile` reads the file path out of the same authoritative `edl` column and
  keeps it for as long as the revision stands: the same ranges now take 6 to 64ms.
- Nothing served a validator, so the browser's media cache could not keep a byte of
  a range response and every element re-read the header from scratch. `fileResponse`
  now sends an `ETag` and `Last-Modified` from the file's size and date, answers a
  matching `If-None-Match` with a 304, and returns the whole file rather than a
  spliced range when `If-Range` no longer matches.
- Nothing mounted early. Each span and each shot now premounts two seconds ahead,
  invisible and frozen on its first frame, so the seek happens while the previous
  one is still playing. Measured at the first splice of a 72s clip: the incoming
  element reaches readyState 4 while still invisible, and 200ms after the cut the
  visible pair is decoded. This is why the span `Sequence` is no longer
  `layout="none"` — Remotion refuses premounting with it, and the wrapper it adds
  instead is an absolute fill of the same source-sized box.
- `pauseWhenBuffering` so a seek that is still not done stops the clock rather than
  playing on over footage nobody saw.

Postmounting the outgoing span to hold its last frame underneath looked like the
obvious fifth thing and was measured doing the opposite: past the end of its own
window the element is below HAVE_FUTURE_DATA, Remotion answers that with `.load()`,
and that resets the element and discards the frame it was being kept for.

Premounting is dropped while rendering, so exports are untouched: tests/*-render
pass unchanged, including the byte-parity of UI, agent and CLI exports of the same
revision. tests/http-file.test.ts holds the validator, the 304 and the stale range.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(jobs): give a project back when the process holding it died

A job row said "running" until the process that owned it wrote the ending. Kill
that process — Ctrl-C, a crash, a `next dev` restart — and the row stayed
running forever, so the project's one-job-at-a-time lock never opened again and
every later edit was refused.

Every process here is local, so liveness is a fact rather than a guess: a job
records its owner's pid and a per-run boot id, and `kill(pid, 0)` answers
whether that process still exists. A heartbeat is only the backstop for a pid
the OS handed to something else. Reaping runs where somebody is already looking
— the project list, the project route, the event stream, the project pages — so
a stuck project heals itself without anybody having to know why. MCP runs in its
own process, so clearing every running row at boot was never an option.

`POST /api/projects/[id]/unlock` is the manual way out when the owning process
is alive but wedged; a run whose project was taken from it no longer writes its
stale ending. The render lock now names its owner too, instead of asking people
to delete `render.lock` by hand after checking `ps`.

`JobState` moves to `lib/job-state.ts` so server code can agree with the browser
without importing the fetch layer.
